旧[[県社]]
[[別表神社]] |創建 = （伝）第8代[[孝元天皇]]年間 |本殿 = [[流造]] |別名 = 八幡宮 |札所等 = |例祭 = [[9月15日]] |神事 = 大頭祭（新嘗祭、[[12月10日]]-[[12月14日|14日]]） |地図 = {{Location map|Japan Nagano|label=武水別神社|float=center|relief=1|width=200|caption=}} {{maplink2|frame=yes|plain=yes|type=point|zoom=12|marker=religious-shinto|frame-align=center|frame-width=200}} }} [[File:Takemizuwake-jinja ootorii.JPG|thumb|200px|right|{{center|大鳥居}}]] '''武水別神社'''（たけみずわけじんじゃ）は、[[長野県]][[千曲市]]八幡にある[[神社]]。[[式内社]]（[[名神大社]]）で、[[信濃国]]四宮井上寛司 『日本中世国家と諸国一宮制』（中世史研究叢書 16） 岩田書院、2009年、55頁。。[[近代社格制度|旧社格]]は[[県社]]で、現在は[[神社本庁]]の[[別表神社]]。 旧称は「'''八幡宮'''」。現在も「八幡さま」「八幡神社」の通称がある。
なお、通称の八幡の読みは、所在地名である千曲市八幡（'''やわた'''）地区と同じ読み方が一般的。 == 祭神 == '''主祭神''' * '''[[武美名別命|武水別大神]]'''（たけみずわけのおおかみ/たけみなわけのおおかみ）祭神は神社由緒書による。 *: 社伝では、善光寺平の豊穣と千曲川の氾濫防止を祈って祀られたとする。 '''相殿神''' : 相殿神は次の3柱で、総じて[[八幡神]]にあたる。 * 誉田別命（ほんだわけのみこと、[[応神天皇]]） * 息長足比売命（おきながたらしひめのみこと、[[神功皇后]]） * [[比売神|比咩大神]]（ひめおおかみ） == 歴史 == === 概史 === 創建年代については社伝によると、第8代[[孝元天皇]]の時代に鎮祭されたという神社由緒書。。 [[六国史|国史]]での初見は[[貞観 (日本)|貞観]]8年（[[866年]]）で、無位から一躍して[[従二位]]の[[神階]]奉授を受けている。また[[延長 (元号)|延長]]5年（[[927年]]）成立の『[[延喜式]]』[[延喜式神名帳|神名帳]]では[[信濃国]][[更級郡]]に「武水別神社 名神大」と記載され、[[名神大社]]に列している。ただしこれらが当社に比定されるに至る根拠は確かではなく『日本の神々』武水別神社項。、他の[[論社]]として[[桶知大神社]]（長野県長野市大岡丙）が挙げられている。 武水別神社一帯は[[平安時代]]末期より[[石清水八幡宮]]の[[荘園 (日本)|荘園]]（小谷荘）となっており、[[安和]]年間（968年-970年）に石清水八幡宮から[[八幡神]]（相殿の3柱）が勧請されたと伝える。八幡神は[[源氏]]の[[氏神]]としても知られ、武水別神社はこの地方随一の[[八幡宮寺]]として広く武門の崇敬を受けた。また[[源義仲|木曾義仲]]が祈願したと伝えられる『参考源平盛衰記』[[養和]]元年（[[1181年]]）6月25日（14日とも）に「八幡社ヲ伏拝ミ」とある。ただし、この「八幡社」が武水別神社と同一かは明らかではない {{Harv|武水別神社（平凡社）|1979年}}。。 [[保元]]3年（[[1158年]]）「更級郡小谷荘等の石清水八幡宮寺及び[[極楽寺]]領、多く[[領家]]、[[預所]]、[[下司]]、[[公文]]等に掠略せらる。是日官宣旨を下して悉く、之を停止せしむ。」（[[石清水文書]]） [[天福 (日本)|天福]]元年（[[1233年]]）「石清水八幡宮寺[[所司]]等更級郡小谷荘[[地頭]]等の、同寺[[安居]][[頭役]]等を解怠すること等を[[朝廷 (日本)|朝廷]]に注進。」（同上） [[応長]]元年（[[1311年]]）「石清水八幡宮寺[[検校]][[善法寺尚清]]、[[権別当]]康清に検校職並びに更級郡小谷荘等の[[所領]]等を譲る。」（同上） [[建武 (日本)|建武]]2年（[[1335年]]）の[[中先代の乱]]では武水別神社[[神官家]]の[[四宮氏]]が[[保科氏]]、[[関屋氏]]、[[夏目氏]]らと共に[[船山守護所]]を襲撃（[[青沼合戦]]）して鎮圧された。これにより隆盛時には地頭と[[郡司]]をも兼ねたと云われる四宮氏は滅び、本八幡の地にあった社殿は焼かれたため現在の地に移転再建されたと伝えられている。 [[応永]]3年（[[1396年]]）更級郡小谷荘八幡神宮寺の梵鐘鋳造。（鐘銘写） [[嘉吉]]8年（[[1443年]]））銘のある銅製灯篭。（[[正平]]21年-[[1367年]]-銘のある[[厳島神社]]の銅製釣灯篭と形が良く似ているとされる。県下で最も年銘の古い優品とされ昭和15年に県宝に指定） [[文明_(日本)|文明]]10年（[[1448年]]）朝廷と[[幕府]]の交流する[[連歌会]]で[[判者]]を務めることもある[[飯尾宗祇]]が[[姨捨山]]の月見に訪れ、時の神官邸で行われた連歌会に参加していたとされる。また文明16年（[[1484年]]）には[[室町幕府]]高官だった[[蜷川氏|蜷川貞相]]が訪れた記録（[[法楽歌|法楽和歌]]）も残されている。 １２年間に５度争われた[[川中島の戦い]]の[[上杉謙信]]の勧請文（[[永禄]]7年[[1567年]]）などが残されている。そして[[武田信玄]]はこの地に[[本陣]]を構えたとも伝えられている。 [[天正]]３年（[[1575年]]）「上杉謙信、更級八幡宮に願文を捧げ[[北条氏政]]の討伐を祈る。」（[[上杉謙信願文集]]） 天正6年（[[1578年]]）「石清水八幡宮、[[蔵坊]]をして、同宮領更級郡小谷荘神領を注進せしむ。石清水八幡宮、同宮領小谷荘神領を注す。」（石清水文書） 天正12年（[[1583年]]）「[[上杉景勝]]、[[松田氏|松田盛直]]に、更級八幡宮社領等を宛行、同郡[[稲荷山]]城に在城せしむ。また、その子、孫三郎をして[[仁科氏|仁科]][[惣領職]]を嗣がしむ。」（[[別本歴代古案]]） [[慶長]]3年（[[1598年]]）「更級八幡宮̪祇官松田盛直、上杉景勝に従い、[[陸奥]][[会津]]に移らんとし、同宮[[神主職]]を同縫殿助に預く。」（[[松田家文書]]） 慶長15年（[[1610年]]）[[海津城]]主[[松平忠輝]]の[[守役]][[大久保石見守]]の寄進奉納した「平面六角形の釣灯篭」（市有形文化財指定） [[慶安]]元年（[[1648年]]）には、[[江戸幕府]]から[[朱印地]]200石を与えられた。 [[文化]]7年（[[1810年]]）社殿等を火災焼失。 [[天保]]8年（[[1837年]]）神主家側から京都[[吉田家]]に働きかけが行われて延喜式内社「武水別神社」の社号を獲得。 [[天保]]13年（[[1842年]]）本殿を含む主要社殿を焼失。 [[嘉永]]3年（[[1850年]]）社殿の再建完成。 [[明治]]元年（[[1868年]]）[[神仏分離令]]。[[松代藩]]への届出や神宮寺側（清水家）に掛け合うなど神主家側が主導して神宮寺は廃絶。それまで[[別当寺]]の支配下で称していた「八幡宮」から「武水別神社」の社名に復した。また、[[近代社格制度]]では当初[[郷社]]に列したが、明治41年（[[1908年]]）に県社に昇格した。 明治12年（[[1876年]]）従来は[[法華八講]]を行う[[仏事|仏教行事]]であった大頭祭が[[神事|神道儀礼]]となり、頭人の首にかけられていた[[数珠]]は[[勾玉]]の頸飾になるなど装束も変更された。 なお、[[1939年]]に[[軍馬|軍用馬]]育成のため施行された種馬統制法により日本在来種の[[木曽馬]]の種馬が廃用処分になった際、同神社の神馬として使役されていた「神明号」は処分を免れた吉永みち子『もっと馬を!』平凡社、1990年、8 - 20ページ「木曽馬の村」。同馬は1950年に民間へ払い下げられ、木曽馬登録事業の1号馬として種雄馬になり、同種の血統復元に貢献した。 === 神階 === * [[貞観 (日本)|貞観]]8年（[[866年]]）6月、無位から従二位 （『[[日本三代実録]]』） - 表記は「武水別神」。 * 貞観9年（[[867年]]）3月26日、官社に列す （『日本三代実録』） - 表記は「武水別神」。 == 境内 == [[File:Takemizuwake-jinja honden.JPG|thumb|210px|right|{{center|本殿}}]] [[File:Takemizuwake-jinja keidai.JPG|thumb|210px|right|{{center|社叢（長野県指定天然記念物）}}]] 18,896平方メートルの社地には、社叢としてケヤキ・スギを主として20数種が生育し、その数は400本を超える。老木も多く、「武水別神社社叢」として昭和４０年に長野県指定天然記念物に指定されている。 南北約280ｍ東西約70ｍの敷地は[[室町時代]]初期と考えられる当地への移転再建当初は正方形であったが東側を[[1742年]]に代表されるような[[千曲川]]による、しばしばの洪水（明治期最大とされる43年の洪水時でも現在の県道界隈は舟で行き来したと伝わる）に削られて現在見る長方形になったと伝えられている。[[寛永]]頃の作成と見られる松田家文書の中に正方形に描かれた境内敷地の図面が最近発見確認された。 現在の社殿の多くは[[天保]]13年（1842年）の火災ののちに建てられたものである。本殿は、[[諏訪]]出身の[[立川和四郎]]（2代目）によって[[嘉永]]3年（1850年）に完成した。拝殿は立川和四郎の後見の下、峰村弥五郎により[[安政]]3年（1856年）に完成。なお、天保13年の火災を免れた社殿として[[摂社]]高良社の本殿がある。 [[別当寺]]の更級八幡神宮寺は[[顕光寺]]・[[善光寺]]・[[津金寺]]・[[光前寺]]と共に[[天台宗]]信濃五山の1つとされていたが、明治の[[廃仏毀釈]]の際に神主家側の主導によって廃寺とされた（月見の寺で名高い[[姨捨]]の[[長楽寺 (千曲市)|長楽寺]]は[[江戸時代]]末の[[善光寺道名所図会]]にはこの神宮寺の支院と説明されていた。このことから長楽寺は更級八幡神宮寺の支配下にあるため「[[田毎月]]」を映す四十八枚田の運用にも極めて強い関与があったものと考えられる）。それまではこの神宮寺僧侶と神社神主によって全ての祭祀を共に行い、境内南半分に仏供所、高良社の向かい側に如法堂、現在の手洗場付近に鐘楼、東側の現在の総代開館には三重の塔があったと伝える。神宮寺廃止後の仏像仏具は秘密裏に[[上山田町]]の東国寺に移されて現存。釈迦堂は解体して筏に組み、千曲川を下り笹崎で陸揚げして土口の正応寺本堂として再建。文書類については近くの大雲寺に移されたが、その後散逸したという。 == 摂末社 == === 摂社 === [[File:Takemizuwake-jinja Kora-sha.JPG|thumb|200px|right|{{center|高良社}}{{small|覆屋内の本殿は長野県宝。}}]] * 高良社（こうらしゃ） *: 覆屋内にある本殿は、境内で最も古く室町時代後期[[16世紀]]頃の造営とされる。一間社[[流造]]の系統に属するが、見世棚造に類似した形式となっている。室町時代の特色を示すものとして、長野県宝に指定されている境内説明板。。 === 末社 === * [[神武天皇]]社 * 疱瘡社 * 酒造租社 * 八剱社 * 宿祢社 * 駒形社 * 荒神社 * 十二神社 * [[天神社]] * 子安社 * 石祠10社：[[御嶽社]]、[[金刀比羅社]]、[[東照宮]]、妙義社、[[岐神|塞ノ神]]、[[道祖神]]、[[水神]]祠、[[山神|山ノ神]]、[[秋葉社]]、[[鹿島社]] == 祭事 == === 年間祭事 === 武水別神社で行われる祭事は次の通り。特に、祈年祭（3月15日）、例大祭（9月15日）、大頭祭（新嘗祭、12月10日-14日）の3祭は「三大祭」と称される。
年間祭事一覧
太字は三大祭祭事は神社由緒書による。。 * 毎月 ** 月次祭 （1日、5日、28日） ** 卯の日祭 （卯の日） * 1月 ** 歳旦祭 （1月1日） ** 御田植祭 （1月5日） ** 越年祭 （1月15日） * 2月 ** 節分祭 （2月節分の日） ** 紀元節祭（建国記念祭） （2月11日） * 3月 ** '''祈年祭''' （3月15日） ** 初卯講祭 （旧暦2月初卯の日） * 4月 ** 日岐目講社祭 （4月中旬） ** 春季祭 （4月28日） * 6月 ** 大祓式 （6月30日） * 7月 ** 柏葉祭 （7月15日） * 9月 ** 八重注連祭 （9月1日） ** 仲秋祭 （9月14日） ** '''例大祭''' （9月15日） ** 秋季祭 （9月24日） * 11月 ** 明治節祭 （11月3日） * 12月 ** 釜清め神事 （12月3日） ** '''大頭祭（新嘗祭）''' （12月10日-14日） ** 天皇誕生祭 （12月23日） ** 大祓式、除夜祭 （12月31日）
=== 大頭祭 === 12月10日から14日に行う[[新嘗祭]]は、「大頭祭（だいとうさい）」と通称される。祭は5人の頭人（とうにん）を中心に進行し、その三番頭を「大頭」と呼ぶことが祭の名前の由来である。歴代の頭人の氏名を記した「御頭帳」では、最古は[[文禄]]元年（1592年）にまで遡っており、400年以上続く祭とされ、国の[[民俗文化財#記録作成等の措置を講ずべき無形の民俗文化財|選択無形民俗文化財]]に選択されている。 == 文化財 == === 選択無形民俗文化財（国選択） === * 武水別神社の頭人行事 - 昭和61年12月17日選択{{国指定文化財等データベース|312|353|武水別神社の頭人行事}}。 === 長野県指定文化財 === * 長野県宝（有形文化財） ** 摂社高良社本殿（建造物） - 室町時代。昭和50年7月21日指定。 ** 銅製釣燈籠（工芸品） - 室町時代。昭和45年4月13日指定。 * 天然記念物 ** 武水別神社社叢 - 昭和40年2月25日指定。 * 史跡 ** 武水別神社松田家館跡 - 中世。現在の所有者は個人。平成18年4月20日指定。 なお神官松田家の建物のうち、松田家住宅主屋が平成16年（2004年）11月22日に、松田家斎館が平成26年（2014年）2月20日にそれぞれ長野県宝（建造物）に指定されていたが、いずれも平成29年（2017年）9月6日に焼失し、平成30年（2018年）2月13日に指定解除されている{{PDFlink|[https://www.pref.nagano.lg.jp/kokai/kensei/kenpo/h30/h3002/documents/kokuji20180213.pdf 平成30年2月13日長野県報]}}より長野県教育委員会告示第1号（リンクは長野県ホームページ）。。 === 千曲市指定文化財 === * 有形文化財[http://www.city.chikuma.lg.jp/docs/2013071800040/ 千曲市文化財一覧]（千曲市ホームページ）。 ** 武水別神社神官松田邸 13棟（建造物） - 江戸時代から明治時代。現在の所有者は千曲市ほか。平成15年2月28日指定。 ** 伎楽面 2面（彫刻） - 金剛面1面、力士面1面の2面。平安時代から鎌倉時代頃。昭和53年3月24日指定。 ** 獅子面 1面（彫刻） - 鎌倉時代。昭和53年3月24日指定。 ** 金銅製六角釣燈篭（工芸品） - 江戸時代。昭和48年3月15日指定。 == 現地情報 == '''所在地''' * [[長野県]][[千曲市]]八幡3012 '''周辺''' * [[稲荷山宿]] - [[善光寺街道]]（[[北国西街道]]、善光寺西街道）の[[宿場]]。 * [[姨捨山]] == 脚注 == '''注釈''' {{reflist|group="注"}} '''出典''' {{reflist|2}} == 参考文献 == * 神社由緒書 * {{Cite book|和書|editor=|author=|year=1979|chapter=武水別神社|title=[[日本歴史地名大系]] 20 長野県の地名|publisher=[[平凡社]]|isbn=4582490204|ref={{Harvid|武水別神社（平凡社）|1979年}}}} * 林幸好「武水別神社」（[[谷川健一]] 編『日本の神々 -神社と聖地- 9 美濃・飛騨・信濃』（[[白水社]]）） == 関連項目 == {{Commonscat|Takemizuwake Shrine}} * [[桶知大神社]]（長野県長野市） - [[式内社]]「武水別神社」の別の論社。 * [[佐良志奈神社]]（若宮八幡宮寺） * [[本八幡]]（もとはちまん）- 968年に石清水八幡宮の分霊がまつられた地と伝わる。 * [[男女離石]]（なめりいし）- 木曾義仲が女人禁制であった八幡宮に戦勝祈願する際に巴御前とここで別れて参拝したと伝わる。以後花嫁行列や新婚夫婦は通行を避けたとの伝承もある。 * [[青沼合戦]]（[[中先代の乱]]） * [[四宮氏]] * [[四宮荘]] * [[小谷荘]] * [[社宮司遺跡]] == 外部リンク == *[https://takemizuwake.jp/ 武水別神社] - 公式サイト * [http://www.furin-kazan.jp/nagano/shiseki/entry/000565.php 武水別神社] - 長野市風林火山特設サイト「川中島の戦い」 * [http://21coe.kokugakuin.ac.jp/db/jinja/241301.html 武水別神社] - 國學院大學21世紀COEプログラム「神道・神社史料集成」 {{神道 横}} {{Normdaten}} {{DEFAULTSORT:たけみすわけしんしや}} [[Category:千曲市の歴史]] [[Category:名神大社]] [[Category:信濃国の式内社|名たけみすわけしんしや]] [[Category:長野県の旧県社]] [[Category:長野県の神社]] [[Category:別表神社]] [[Category:長野県宝]] [[Category:長野県指定天然記念物]] [[Category:長野県内の市町村指定有形文化財]] [[Category:八幡宮]] [[Category:千曲市の建築物]]

{{Infobox religious building|religious_affiliation = [[Shinto]]|religious_affiliation = [[Shinto]]|religious_affiliation = [[Shinto]]| religious_affiliation = [[Shinto]] | name = Takemizuwake Shrine | image = Takemizuwake-jinja shaden.JPG |caption = From right: Chokushiden, Haiden, Honden | location = {{ill|Chikuma, Nagano|ja|千曲市}}, Nagano Prefecture, Japan | coordinates = {{coord|36|31|10.08|N|138|06|10.71|E|region:JP-20_type:landmark|display=inline,title|name=Takemizuwake Shrine}} | deity = {{ill|Takemizuwake no Ōkami|ja|武美名別命}} | object = | type = {{ill|Shikinai-sha|ja|式内社}} ({{ill|Myojin Taisha|ja|名神大}})
Fourth shrine of {{ill|Shinano Province|ja|信濃国}}
Former {{ill|Prefectural shrine|ja|県社}}
{{ill|Beppyo Shrine|ja|別表神社}} | established = During the reign of the 8th Emperor {{ill|Emperor Kōgen|ja|孝元天皇}} (trad.) | architecture = Nagare-zukuri | nickname = Hachiman Shrine | pilgrimage = | festival = September 15 | rituals = Daitōsai (Niinamesai), December 10-14 | map = Japan Nagano Prefecture | label = Takemizuwake Shrine | relief = 1 | map_width = 256 }} [[File:Takemizuwake-jinja ootorii.JPG|thumb|200px|right|{{center|Ōtorii}}]] '''Takemizuwake Shrine''' (武水別神社[[ja:武水別神社]]) is a {{ill|Shinto shrine|ja|神社}} located in {{ill|Chikuma, Nagano|ja|千曲市}}, Nagano Prefecture, Japan. It is a {{ill|Shikinai-sha|ja|式内社}} ({{ill|Myojin Taisha|ja|名神大}}) and the fourth shrine of {{ill|Shinano Province|ja|信濃国}}. It was formerly classified as a {{ill|Prefectural shrine|ja|県社}} and is now a {{ill|Beppyo Shrine|ja|別表神社}} under the Association of Shinto Shrines. The shrine's old name was "Hachiman Shrine," and it is still commonly referred to as "Yawata-sama" or "Yawata Shrine." == deity == '''Main deity''' * '''{{ill|Takemizuwake no Ōkami|ja|武美名別命}}''' (Takemizuwake no Ōkami)According to the shrine's history. *: The shrine's tradition states that this deity was enshrined to pray for the fertility of the Zenkoji Plain and to prevent the flooding of the Chikuma River. '''Deities in the Same Shrine''' : The three deities enshrined together here collectively represent the {{ill|Hachiman|lt=Hachiman deity|ja|八幡神}}. * [[Emperor Ōjin|Hondawake-no-Mikoto]] (誉田別命, {{ill|Emperor Ōjin|ja|応神天皇}}) * Okinagatarashihime no Mikoto (息長足比売命, {{ill|Empress Jingū|ja|神功皇后}}) * Hime Ōkami (比咩大神) == History == === Overview === According to shrine tradition, it was established during the reign of the 8th Emperor {{ill|Emperor Kōgen|ja|孝元天皇}}Shrine history.. The earliest record in historical documents is from {{ill|Jogan|ja|貞観}} 8 (866), when it was given the rank of {{ill|Junior Second rank|ja|従二位|1=Junior Second Rank}} from no rank. Additionally, it is listed as "Takemizuwake Shrine" in the {{ill|Engishiki|ja|延喜式}} compiled in {{ill|Engi|ja|延長}} 5 (927), categorized as a {{ill|Myojin Taisha|ja|名神大}}. However, the evidence supporting the identification of this shrine as the one mentioned in the documents is not definitive『日本の神々』 Takemizuwake Shrine entry., and another candidate is {{ill|Okeno Omi Shrine|ja|桶知大神社}} in Nagano City. The area around Takemizuwake Shrine became an estate ({{ill|Shōen|ja|荘園}}) of {{ill|Iwashimizu Hachimangū|ja|石清水八幡宮}} (Otani estate) from the late Heian period, and it is said that the Hachiman deity (the three deities enshrined together) was invited from Iwashimizu Hachimangū during the Anwa era (968-970). The Hachiman deity is known as the tutelary deity of the {{ill|Minamoto clan|ja|源氏}}, and Takemizuwake Shrine was widely revered by warriors as the foremost Hachiman Shrine in the region. It is also said that {{ill|Minamoto no Yoshinaka|ja|源義仲}} prayed here『参考源平盛衰記』 mentions on June 25 (or 14), Yōwa 1 (1181), that "八幡社ヲ伏拝ミ". However, it is unclear if this "Hachiman Shrine" is the same as Takemizuwake Shrine.. In {{ill|:en:Hōgen (era)|lt=Hōgen|ja|保元}} 3 (1158), there is a record of lands in Otani estate, Sarashina District being confiscated by multiple officials. On that day, a government order was issued to halt thisIwashimizu document. During the {{ill|Nanboku-chō period|ja|南北朝時代}} (1335), the Four Shrine clan, who served as Shinto priests of Takemizuwake Shrine, together with the Hoshina and Sekiya clans, attacked the {{ill|Shugo|ja|守護所}} (provincial headquarters) in Funeiyama (Suwa), but were suppressed. This resulted in the downfall of the Four Shrine clan, who were said to have served as both {{ill|Jitō|ja|地頭}} and district officials during their peak. The shrine buildings were burned down and later rebuilt at their current location. In {{ill|Tenshō|ja|天正}} 3 (1575), {{ill|Uesugi Kenshin|ja|上杉謙信}} offered a prayer document to the shrine, praying for victory against {{ill|Hōjō Ujizane|ja|北条氏政}}{{ill|Uesugi Kenshin prayer document|ja|上杉謙信願文集}}. In {{ill|Kanei|ja|寛永}} 1 (1624), the Tokugawa shogunate granted 200 koku of shrine land to the shrine. In Meiji 1 (1868), following the separation of Shinto and Buddhism ({{ill|Shinbutsu bunri|ja|神仏分離}}), the shrine was renamed "Takemizuwake Shrine" from "Hachiman Shrine," reflecting the disbanding of the associated temple ({{ill|Shinano Five Mountains|ja|信濃五山}}). The shrine was initially classified as a village shrine ({{ill|Gōsha|ja|郷社}}) in the Modern Shrine ranking System but was promoted to a prefectural shrine ([[Ken-sha]]) in Meiji 41 (1908). In 1876, the traditional Buddhist ceremony, the Grand Head festival ({{ill|Daitōsai|ja|大頭祭}}), was transformed into a Shinto ritual吉永みち子『もっと馬を!』平凡社、1990年、8 - 20ページ「木曽馬の村」. === Shrine ranks === * Jogan 8 (866) June, promoted from no rank to Junior Second rank (『{{ill|Nihon Sandai Jitsuroku|ja|日本三代実録}}』) * Jogan 9 (867) March 26, listed as a government shrine (『日本三代実録』) == Shrine Grounds == [[File:Takemizuwake-jinja honden.JPG|thumb|210px|right|{{center|Honden}}]] [[File:Takemizuwake-jinja keidai.JPG|thumb|210px|right|{{center|Shrine Grove (Nagano Prefecture designated natural monument)}}]] The shrine grounds cover 18,896 square meters and include a grove primarily composed of zelkova and cedar trees, with over 20 species and 400 trees in total. Many of the trees are old, and the "Takemizuwake Shrine Grove" is designated as a natural monument by Nagano Prefecture. The grounds, measuring approximately 280 meters from north to south and 70 meters from east to west, were originally square but were eroded into their current rectangular shape by frequent floods from the Chikuma River. A document from the Kanei era (1624-1644) was recently discovered, showing a square layout. Most of the current shrine buildings were constructed after a fire in Tenpō 13 (1842). The main hall was completed in Kaei 3 (1850) by Tatekawa Washiro II from Suwa. The worship hall was completed in Ansei 3 (1856) by Mineura Yagorō under Tatekawa Washiro's supervision. The main hall of the subsidiary Kōra Shrine is the oldest building, having survived the fire. The associated temple, known as Sarashina Hachiman Jinguji, was one of the Shinano Five Mountains of the Tendai sect but was abolished during the Meiji period's anti-Buddhist movement ({{ill|Haibutsu kishaku|ja|廃仏毀釈}}). == Subsidiary Shrines == === Subsidiary Shrines === [[File:Takemizuwake-jinja Kora-sha.JPG|thumb|200px|right|{{center|Kōra Shrine}}{{small|The main hall inside the covering structure is a Nagano Prefecture treasure.}}]] * Kōra Shrine (高良社) *: The main hall inside the covering structure is the oldest in the shrine grounds, believed to have been built in the late Muromachi period (16th century). It is designated as a Nagano Prefecture treasureExplanatory panel on-site.. === Associated Shrines === * Emperor Jimmu Shrine * Smallpox Shrine * Sake Brewer Shrine * Yaegaki Shrine * Sukune Shrine * Komagata Shrine * Kojin Shrine * Twelve Shrines * Tenjin Shrine * Koyasu Shrine * Ten stone shrines: Ontake Shrine, Kotohira Shrine, Tōshōgū, Myōgi Shrine, Seki no Kami, Dōsojin, Water God Shrine, Mountain God Shrine, Akiba Shrine, Kashima Shrine == festivals == === festivals === The festivals held at Takemizuwake Shrine are as follows. Particularly notable are the three major festivals: the Prayer festival (March 15), the Grand festival (September 15), and the Grand Head festival (New Harvest festival, December 10-14).
festivals List
The three major festivals are in boldfestivals according to the shrine history.. * Monthly ** Monthly festival (1st, 5th, 28th) ** Usagi Day festival (Usagi Day) * January ** New Year's festival (January 1) ** Rice Planting festival (January 5) ** New Year's festival (January 15) * February ** Setsubun festival (Setsubun Day in February) ** National Foundation Day festival (February 11) * March ** '''Prayer festival''' (March 15) ** First Usagi Lecture festival (Old Calendar February Usagi Day) * April ** Higime Lecture Society festival (Mid-April) ** Spring festival (April 28) * June ** Great Purification ceremony (June 30) * July ** Kashiwa festival (July 15) * September ** Yaejime festival (September 1) ** Mid-Autumn festival (September 14) ** '''Grand festival''' (September 15) ** Autumn festival (September 24) * November ** Meiji Day festival (November 3) * December ** Kama Purification Ritual (December 3) ** '''Grand Head festival (New Harvest festival)''' (December 10-14) ** Emperor's Birthday festival (December 23) ** Great Purification ceremony, New Year's Eve festival (December 31)
=== Grand Head festival === The Grand Head festival (Niinamesai) held from December 10 to 14 is called the "Daitōsai". The festival is led by five headmen, with the third headman being called "Daitō," giving the festival its name. The "Headman's Record" (御頭帳) traces back to Bunroku 1 (1592), making it a festival with a history of over 400 years. It is designated as an Important Intangible Folk Cultural Property of Japan. == Cultural Properties == === Selected Intangible Folk Cultural Property (National Selection) === * Headman's ceremony of Takemizuwake Shrine - Selected on December 17, 1986{{Cultural Property Database|312|353|Headman's ceremony of Takemizuwake Shrine}}. === Nagano Prefecture Designated Cultural Properties === * Nagano Prefecture Treasures (Tangible Cultural Properties) ** main hall of Kōra Shrine (Building) - Muromachi period. Designated on July 21, 1975. ** Bronze Hanging Lantern (Craft) - Muromachi period. {{Infobox religious building|religious_affiliation = [[Shinto]]|religious_affiliation = [[Shinto]]|religious_affiliation = [[Shinto]]| religious_affiliation = [[Shinto]] | name = Takemizuwake Shrine | image = Takemizuwake-jinja shaden.JPG |caption = From right: Chokushiden, Haiden, Honden | location = {{ill|Chikuma, Nagano|ja|千曲市}}, Nagano Prefecture, Japan | coordinates = {{coord|36|31|10.08|N|138|06|10.71|E|region:JP-20_type:landmark|display=inline,title|name=Takemizuwake Shrine}} | deity = {{ill|Takemizuwake no Ōkami|ja|武美名別命}} | object = | type = {{ill|Shikinai-sha|ja|式内社}} ({{ill|Myojin Taisha|ja|名神大}})
Fourth shrine of {{ill|Shinano Province|ja|信濃国}}
Former {{ill|Prefectural shrine|ja|県社}}
{{ill|Beppyo Shrine|ja|別表神社}} | established = During the reign of the 8th Emperor {{ill|Emperor Kōgen|ja|孝元天皇}} (trad.) | architecture = Nagare-zukuri | nickname = Hachiman Shrine | pilgrimage = | festival = September 15 | rituals = Daitōsai (Niinamesai), December 10-14 | map = Japan Nagano Prefecture | label = Takemizuwake Shrine | relief = 1 | map_width = 256 }} [[File:Takemizuwake-jinja ootorii.JPG|thumb|200px|right|{{center|Ōtorii}}]] '''Takemizuwake Shrine''' (武水別神社[[ja:武水別神社]]) is a {{ill|Shinto shrine|ja|神社}} located in {{ill|Chikuma, Nagano|ja|千曲市}}, Nagano Prefecture, Japan. It is a {{ill|Shikinai-sha|ja|式内社}} ({{ill|Myojin Taisha|ja|名神大}}) and the fourth shrine of {{ill|Shinano Province|ja|信濃国}}. It was formerly classified as a {{ill|Prefectural shrine|ja|県社}} and is now a {{ill|Beppyo Shrine|ja|別表神社}} under the Association of Shinto Shrines. The shrine's old name was "Hachiman Shrine," and it is still commonly referred to as "Yawata-sama" or "Yawata Shrine." == deity == '''Main deity''' * '''{{ill|Takemizuwake no Ōkami|ja|武美名別命}}''' (Takemizuwake no Ōkami)According to the shrine's history. *: The shrine's tradition states that this deity was enshrined to pray for the fertility of the Zenkoji Plain and to prevent the flooding of the Chikuma River. '''Deities in the Same Shrine''' : The three deities enshrined together here collectively represent the {{ill|Hachiman|lt=Hachiman deity|ja|八幡神}}. * [[Emperor Ōjin|Hondawake-no-Mikoto]] (誉田別命, {{ill|Emperor Ōjin|ja|応神天皇}}) * Okinagatarashihime no Mikoto (息長足比売命, {{ill|Empress Jingū|ja|神功皇后}}) * Hime Ōkami (比咩大神) == History == === Overview === According to shrine tradition, it was established during the reign of the 8th Emperor {{ill|Emperor Kōgen|ja|孝元天皇}}Shrine history.. The earliest record in historical documents is from {{ill|Jogan|ja|貞観}} 8 (866), when it was given the rank of {{ill|Junior Second rank|ja|従二位|1=Junior Second Rank}} from no rank. Additionally, it is listed as "Takemizuwake Shrine" in the {{ill|Engishiki|ja|延喜式}} compiled in {{ill|Engi|ja|延長}} 5 (927), categorized as a {{ill|Myojin Taisha|ja|名神大}}. However, the evidence supporting the identification of this shrine as the one mentioned in the documents is not definitive『日本の神々』 Takemizuwake Shrine entry., and another candidate is {{ill|Okeno Omi Shrine|ja|桶知大神社}} in Nagano City. The area around Takemizuwake Shrine became an estate ({{ill|Shōen|ja|荘園}}) of {{ill|Iwashimizu Hachimangū|ja|石清水八幡宮}} (Otani estate) from the late Heian period, and it is said that the Hachiman deity (the three deities enshrined together) was invited from Iwashimizu Hachimangū during the Anwa era (968-970). The Hachiman deity is known as the tutelary deity of the {{ill|Minamoto clan|ja|源氏}}, and Takemizuwake Shrine was widely revered by warriors as the foremost Hachiman Shrine in the region. It is also said that {{ill|Minamoto no Yoshinaka|ja|源義仲}} prayed here『参考源平盛衰記』 mentions on June 25 (or 14), Yōwa 1 (1181), that "八幡社ヲ伏拝ミ". However, it is unclear if this "Hachiman Shrine" is the same as Takemizuwake Shrine.. In {{ill|:en:Hōgen (era)|lt=Hōgen|ja|保元}} 3 (1158), there is a record of lands in Otani estate, Sarashina District being confiscated by multiple officials. On that day, a government order was issued to halt thisIwashimizu document. During the {{ill|Nanboku-chō period|ja|南北朝時代}} (1335), the Four Shrine clan, who served as Shinto priests of Takemizuwake Shrine, together with the Hoshina and Sekiya clans, attacked the {{ill|Shugo|ja|守護所}} (provincial headquarters) in Funeiyama (Suwa), but were suppressed. This resulted in the downfall of the Four Shrine clan, who were said to have served as both {{ill|Jitō|ja|地頭}} and district officials during their peak. The shrine buildings were burned down and later rebuilt at their current location. In {{ill|Tenshō|ja|天正}} 3 (1575), {{ill|Uesugi Kenshin|ja|上杉謙信}} offered a prayer document to the shrine, praying for victory against {{ill|Hōjō Ujizane|ja|北条氏政}}{{ill|Uesugi Kenshin prayer document|ja|上杉謙信願文集}}. In {{ill|Kanei|ja|寛永}} 1 (1624), the Tokugawa shogunate granted 200 koku of shrine land to the shrine. In Meiji 1 (1868), following the separation of Shinto and Buddhism ({{ill|Shinbutsu bunri|ja|神仏分離}}), the shrine was renamed "Takemizuwake Shrine" from "Hachiman Shrine," reflecting the disbanding of the associated temple ({{ill|Shinano Five Mountains|ja|信濃五山}}). The shrine was initially classified as a village shrine ({{ill|Gōsha|ja|郷社}}) in the Modern Shrine ranking System but was promoted to a prefectural shrine ([[Ken-sha]]) in Meiji 41 (1908). In 1876, the traditional Buddhist ceremony, the Grand Head festival ({{ill|Daitōsai|ja|大頭祭}}), was transformed into a Shinto ritual吉永みち子『もっと馬を!』平凡社、1990年、8 - 20ページ「木曽馬の村」. === Shrine ranks === * Jogan 8 (866) June, promoted from no rank to Junior Second rank (『{{ill|Nihon Sandai Jitsuroku|ja|日本三代実録}}』) * Jogan 9 (867) March 26, listed as a government shrine (『日本三代実録』) == Shrine Grounds == [[File:Takemizuwake-jinja honden.JPG|thumb|210px|right|{{center|Honden}}]] [[File:Takemizuwake-jinja keidai.JPG|thumb|210px|right|{{center|Shrine Grove (Nagano Prefecture designated natural monument)}}]] The shrine grounds cover 18,896 square meters and include a grove primarily composed of zelkova and cedar trees, with over 20 species and 400 trees in total. Many of the trees are old, and the "Takemizuwake Shrine Grove" is designated as a natural monument by Nagano Prefecture. The grounds, measuring approximately 280 meters from north to south and 70 meters from east to west, were originally square but were eroded into their current rectangular shape by frequent floods from the Chikuma River. A document from the Kanei era (1624-1644) was recently discovered, showing a square layout. Most of the current shrine buildings were constructed after a fire in Tenpō 13 (1842). The main hall was completed in Kaei 3 (1850) by Tatekawa Washiro II from Suwa. The worship hall was completed in Ansei 3 (1856) by Mineura Yagorō under Tatekawa Washiro's supervision. The main hall of the subsidiary Kōra Shrine is the oldest building, having survived the fire. The associated temple, known as Sarashina Hachiman Jinguji, was one of the Shinano Five Mountains of the Tendai sect but was abolished during the Meiji period's anti-Buddhist movement ({{ill|Haibutsu kishaku|ja|廃仏毀釈}}). == Subsidiary Shrines == === Subsidiary Shrines === [[File:Takemizuwake-jinja Kora-sha.JPG|thumb|200px|right|{{center|Kōra Shrine}}{{small|The main hall inside the covering structure is a Nagano Prefecture treasure.}}]] * Kōra Shrine (高良社) *: The main hall inside the covering structure is the oldest in the shrine grounds, believed to have been built in the late Muromachi period (16th century). It is designated as a Nagano Prefecture treasureExplanatory panel on-site.. === Associated Shrines === * Emperor Jimmu Shrine * Smallpox Shrine * Sake Brewer Shrine * Yaegaki Shrine * Sukune Shrine * Komagata Shrine * Kojin Shrine * Twelve Shrines * Tenjin Shrine * Koyasu Shrine * Ten stone shrines: Ontake Shrine, Kotohira Shrine, Tōshōgū, Myōgi Shrine, Seki no Kami, Dōsojin, Water God Shrine, Mountain God Shrine, Akiba Shrine, Kashima Shrine == festivals == === festivals === The festivals held at Takemizuwake Shrine are as follows. Particularly notable are the three major festivals: the Prayer festival (March 15), the Grand festival (September 15), and the Grand Head festival (New Harvest festival, December 10-14).
festivals List
The three major festivals are in boldfestivals according to the shrine history.. * Monthly ** Monthly festival (1st, 5th, 28th) ** Usagi Day festival (Usagi Day) * January ** New Year's festival (January 1) ** Rice Planting festival (January 5) ** New Year's festival (January 15) * February ** Setsubun festival (Setsubun Day in February) ** National Foundation Day festival (February 11) * March ** '''Prayer festival''' (March 15) ** First Usagi Lecture festival (Old Calendar February Usagi Day) * April ** Higime Lecture Society festival (Mid-April) ** Spring festival (April 28) * June ** Great Purification ceremony (June 30) * July ** Kashiwa festival (July 15) * September ** Yaejime festival (September 1) ** Mid-Autumn festival (September 14) ** '''Grand festival''' (September 15) ** Autumn festival (September 24) * November ** Meiji Day festival (November 3) * December ** Kama Purification Ritual (December 3) ** '''Grand Head festival (New Harvest festival)''' (December 10-14) ** Emperor's Birthday festival (December 23) ** Great Purification ceremony, New Year's Eve festival (December 31)
=== Grand Head festival === The Grand Head festival (Niinamesai) held from December 10 to 14 is called the "Daitōsai". The festival is led by five headmen, with the third headman being called "Daitō," giving the festival its name. The "Headman's Record" (御頭帳) traces back to Bunroku 1 (1592), making it a festival with a history of over 400 years. It is designated as an Important Intangible Folk Cultural Property of Japan. == Cultural Properties == === Selected Intangible Folk Cultural Property (National Selection) === * Headman's ceremony of Takemizuwake Shrine - Selected on December 17, 1986{{Cultural Property Database|312|353|Headman's ceremony of Takemizuwake Shrine}}. === Nagano Prefecture Designated Cultural Properties === * Nagano Prefecture Treasures (Tangible Cultural Properties) ** main hall of Kōra Shrine (Building) - Muromachi period. In {{ill|:en:Hōgen (era)|lt=Hōgen|ja|保元}} 3 (1158), there is a record of lands in Otani estate, Sarashina District being confiscated by multiple officials. This resulted in the downfall of the Four Shrine clan, who were said to have served as both {{ill|Jitō|ja|地頭}} and district officials during their peak. The shrine buildings were burned down and later rebuilt at their current location. In {{ill|Kanei|ja|寛永}} 1 (1624), the Tokugawa shogunate granted 200 koku of shrine land to the shrine. In Meiji 1 (1868), following the separation of Shinto and Buddhism ({{ill|Shinbutsu bunri|ja|神仏分離}}), the shrine was renamed "Takemizuwake Shrine" from "Hachiman Shrine," reflecting the disbanding of the associated temple ({{ill|Shinano Five Mountains|ja|信濃五山}}). The shrine was initially classified as a village shrine ({{ill|Gōsha|ja|郷社}}) in the Modern Shrine ranking System but was promoted to a prefectural shrine ([[Ken-sha]]) in Meiji 41 (1908). In 1876, the traditional Buddhist ceremony, the Grand Head festival ({{ill|Daitōsai|ja|大頭祭}}), was transformed into a Shinto ritual吉永みち子『もっと馬を!』平凡社、1990年、8 - 20ページ「木曽馬の村」. === Shrine ranks === * Jogan 8 (866) June, promoted from no rank to Junior Second rank (『{{ill|Nihon Sandai Jitsuroku|ja|日本三代実録}}』) * Jogan 9 (867) March 26, listed as a government shrine (『日本三代実録』) == Shrine Grounds == [[File:Takemizuwake-jinja honden.JPG|thumb|210px|right|{{center|Honden}}]] [[File:Takemizuwake-jinja keidai.JPG|thumb|210px|right|{{center|Shrine Grove (Nagano Prefecture designated natural monument)}}]] The shrine grounds cover 18,896 square meters and include a grove primarily composed of zelkova and cedar trees, with over 20 species and 400 trees in total. Many of the trees are old, and the "Takemizuwake Shrine Grove" is designated as a natural monument by Nagano Prefecture. The grounds, measuring approximately 280 meters from north to south and 70 meters from east to west, were originally square but were eroded into their current rectangular shape by frequent floods from the Chikuma River. A document from the Kanei era (1624-1644) was recently discovered, showing a square layout. Most of the current shrine buildings were constructed after a fire in Tenpō 13 (1842). The main hall was completed in Kaei 3 (1850) by Tatekawa Washiro II from Suwa. The worship hall was completed in Ansei 3 (1856) by Mineura Yagorō under Tatekawa Washiro's supervision. The main hall of the subsidiary Kōra Shrine is the oldest building, having survived the fire. The associated temple, known as Sarashina Hachiman Jinguji, was one of the Shinano Five Mountains of the Tendai sect but was abolished during the Meiji period's anti-Buddhist movement ({{ill|Haibutsu kishaku|ja|廃仏毀釈}}). == Subsidiary Shrines == === Subsidiary Shrines === [[File:Takemizuwake-jinja Kora-sha.JPG|thumb|200px|right|{{center|Kōra Shrine}}{{small|The main hall inside the covering structure is a Nagano Prefecture treasure.}}]] * Kōra Shrine (高良社) *: The main hall inside the covering structure is the oldest in the shrine grounds, believed to have been built in the late Muromachi period (16th century). It was formerly classified as a {{ill|Prefectural shrine|ja|県社}} and is now a {{ill|Beppyo Shrine|ja|別表神社}} under the Association of Shinto Shrines. {{Infobox religious building|religious_affiliation = [[Shinto]]|religious_affiliation = [[Shinto]]|religious_affiliation = [[Shinto]]| religious_affiliation = [[Shinto]] | name = Takemizuwake Shrine | image = Takemizuwake-jinja shaden.JPG |caption = From right: Chokushiden, Haiden, Honden | location = {{ill|Chikuma, Nagano|ja|千曲市}}, Nagano Prefecture, Japan | coordinates = {{coord|36|31|10.08|N|138|06|10.71|E|region:JP-20_type:landmark|display=inline,title|name=Takemizuwake Shrine}} | deity = {{ill|Takemizuwake no Ōkami|ja|武美名別命}} | object = | type = {{ill|Shikinai-sha|ja|式内社}} ({{ill|Myojin Taisha|ja|名神大}})

Former {{ill|Prefectural shrine|ja|県社}}
{{ill|Beppyo Shrine|ja|別表神社}} | established = During the reign of the 8th Emperor {{ill|Emperor Kōgen|ja|孝元天皇}} (trad.) | architecture = Nagare-zukuri | nickname = Hachiman Shrine | pilgrimage = | festival = September 15 | rituals = Daitōsai (Niinamesai), December 10-14 | map = Japan Nagano Prefecture | label = Takemizuwake Shrine | relief = 1 | map_width = 256 }} [[File:Takemizuwake-jinja ootorii.JPG|thumb|200px|right|{{center|Ōtorii}}]] '''Takemizuwake Shrine''' (武水別神社[[ja:武水別神社]]) is a {{ill|Shinto shrine|ja|神社}} located in {{ill|Chikuma, Nagano|ja|千曲市}}, Nagano Prefecture, Japan. It is a {{ill|Shikinai-sha|ja|式内社}} ({{ill|Myojin Taisha|ja|名神大}}) and the fourth shrine of {{ill|Shinano Province|ja|信濃国}}. It was formerly classified as a {{ill|Prefectural shrine|ja|県社}} and is now a {{ill|Beppyo Shrine|ja|別表神社}} under the Association of Shinto Shrines. The shrine's old name was "Hachiman Shrine," and it is still commonly referred to as "Yawata-sama" or "Yawata Shrine." == deity == '''Main deity''' * '''{{ill|Takemizuwake no Ōkami|ja|武美名別命}}''' (Takemizuwake no Ōkami)According to the shrine's history. *: The shrine's tradition states that this deity was enshrined to pray for the fertility of the Zenkoji Plain and to prevent the flooding of the Chikuma River. '''Deities in the Same Shrine''' : The three deities enshrined together here collectively represent the {{ill|Hachiman|lt=Hachiman deity|ja|八幡神}}. * [[Emperor Ōjin|Hondawake-no-Mikoto]] (誉田別命, {{ill|Emperor Ōjin|ja|応神天皇}}) * Okinagatarashihime no Mikoto (息長足比売命, {{ill|Empress Jingū|ja|神功皇后}}) * Hime Ōkami (比咩大神) == History == === Overview === According to shrine tradition, it was established during the reign of the 8th Emperor {{ill|Emperor Kōgen|ja|孝元天皇}}Shrine history.. The earliest record in historical documents is from {{ill|Jogan|ja|貞観}} 8 (866), when it was given the rank of {{ill|Junior Second rank|ja|従二位|1=Junior Second Rank}} from no rank. Additionally, it is listed as "Takemizuwake Shrine" in the {{ill|Engishiki|ja|延喜式}} compiled in {{ill|Engi|ja|延長}} 5 (927), categorized as a {{ill|Myojin Taisha|ja|名神大}}. However, the evidence supporting the identification of this shrine as the one mentioned in the documents is not definitive『日本の神々』 Takemizuwake Shrine entry., and another candidate is {{ill|Okeno Omi Shrine|ja|桶知大神社}} in Nagano City. The area around Takemizuwake Shrine became an estate ({{ill|Shōen|ja|荘園}}) of {{ill|Iwashimizu Hachimangū|ja|石清水八幡宮}} (Otani estate) from the late Heian period, and it is said that the Hachiman deity (the three deities enshrined together) was invited from Iwashimizu Hachimangū during the Anwa era (968-970). The Hachiman deity is known as the tutelary deity of the {{ill|Minamoto clan|ja|源氏}}, and Takemizuwake Shrine was widely revered by warriors as the foremost Hachiman Shrine in the region. It is also said that {{ill|Minamoto no Yoshinaka|ja|源義仲}} prayed here『参考源平盛衰記』 mentions on June 25 (or 14), Yōwa 1 (1181), that "八幡社ヲ伏拝ミ". However, it is unclear if this "Hachiman Shrine" is the same as Takemizuwake Shrine.. In {{ill|:en:Hōgen (era)|lt=Hōgen|ja|保元}} 3 (1158), there is a record of lands in Otani estate, Sarashina District being confiscated by multiple officials. On that day, a government order was issued to halt thisIwashimizu document. During the {{ill|Nanboku-chō period|ja|南北朝時代}} (1335), the Four Shrine clan, who served as Shinto priests of Takemizuwake Shrine, together with the Hoshina and Sekiya clans, attacked the {{ill|Shugo|ja|守護所}} (provincial headquarters) in Funeiyama (Suwa), but were suppressed. This resulted in the downfall of the Four Shrine clan, who were said to have served as both {{ill|Jitō|ja|地頭}} and district officials during their peak. The shrine buildings were burned down and later rebuilt at their current location. In {{ill|Tenshō|ja|天正}} 3 (1575), {{ill|Uesugi Kenshin|ja|上杉謙信}} offered a prayer document to the shrine, praying for victory against {{ill|Hōjō Ujizane|ja|北条氏政}}{{ill|Uesugi Kenshin prayer document|ja|上杉謙信願文集}}. In {{ill|Kanei|ja|寛永}} 1 (1624), the Tokugawa shogunate granted 200 koku of shrine land to the shrine. In Meiji 1 (1868), following the separation of Shinto and Buddhism ({{ill|Shinbutsu bunri|ja|神仏分離}}), the shrine was renamed "Takemizuwake Shrine" from "Hachiman Shrine," reflecting the disbanding of the associated temple ({{ill|Shinano Five Mountains|ja|信濃五山}}). The shrine was initially classified as a village shrine ({{ill|Gōsha|ja|郷社}}) in the Modern Shrine ranking System but was promoted to a prefectural shrine ([[Ken-sha]]) in Meiji 41 (1908). In 1876, the traditional Buddhist ceremony, the Grand Head festival ({{ill|Daitōsai|ja|大頭祭}}), was transformed into a Shinto ritual吉永みち子『もっと馬を!』平凡社、1990年、8 - 20ページ「木曽馬の村」. === Shrine ranks === * Jogan 8 (866) June, promoted from no rank to Junior Second rank (『{{ill|Nihon Sandai Jitsuroku|ja|日本三代実録}}』) * Jogan 9 (867) March 26, listed as a government shrine (『日本三代実録』) == Shrine Grounds == [[File:Takemizuwake-jinja honden.JPG|thumb|210px|right|{{center|Honden}}]] [[File:Takemizuwake-jinja keidai.JPG|thumb|210px|right|{{center|Shrine Grove (Nagano Prefecture designated natural monument)}}]] The shrine grounds cover 18,896 square meters and include a grove primarily composed of zelkova and cedar trees, with over 20 species and 400 trees in total. Many of the trees are old, and the "Takemizuwake Shrine Grove" is designated as a natural monument by Nagano Prefecture. The grounds, measuring approximately 280 meters from north to south and 70 meters from east to west, were originally square but were eroded into their current rectangular shape by frequent floods from the Chikuma River. A document from the Kanei era (1624-1644) was recently discovered, showing a square layout. Most of the current shrine buildings were constructed after a fire in Tenpō 13 (1842). The main hall was completed in Kaei 3 (1850) by Tatekawa Washiro II from Suwa. The worship hall was completed in Ansei 3 (1856) by Mineura Yagorō under Tatekawa Washiro's supervision. The main hall of the subsidiary Kōra Shrine is the oldest building, having survived the fire. The associated temple, known as Sarashina Hachiman Jinguji, was one of the Shinano Five Mountains of the Tendai sect but was abolished during the Meiji period's anti-Buddhist movement ({{ill|Haibutsu kishaku|ja|廃仏毀釈}}). == Subsidiary Shrines == === Subsidiary Shrines === [[File:Takemizuwake-jinja Kora-sha.JPG|thumb|200px|right|{{center|Kōra Shrine}}{{small|The main hall inside the covering structure is a Nagano Prefecture treasure.}}]] * Kōra Shrine (高良社) *: The main hall inside the covering structure is the oldest in the shrine grounds, believed to have been built in the late Muromachi period (16th century). It is designated as a Nagano Prefecture treasureExplanatory panel on-site.. === Associated Shrines === * Emperor Jimmu Shrine * Smallpox Shrine * Sake Brewer Shrine * Yaegaki Shrine * Sukune Shrine * Komagata Shrine * Kojin Shrine * Twelve Shrines * Tenjin Shrine * Koyasu Shrine * Ten stone shrines: Ontake Shrine, Kotohira Shrine, Tōshōgū, Myōgi Shrine, Seki no Kami, Dōsojin, Water God Shrine, Mountain God Shrine, Akiba Shrine, Kashima Shrine == festivals == === festivals === The festivals held at Takemizuwake Shrine are as follows. Particularly notable are the three major festivals: the Prayer festival (March 15), the Grand festival (September 15), and the Grand Head festival (New Harvest festival, December 10-14).
festivals List
The three major festivals are in boldfestivals according to the shrine history.. * Monthly ** Monthly festival (1st, 5th, 28th) ** Usagi Day festival (Usagi Day) * January ** New Year's festival (January 1) ** Rice Planting festival (January 5) ** New Year's festival (January 15) * February ** Setsubun festival (Setsubun Day in February) ** National Foundation Day festival (February 11) * March ** '''Prayer festival''' (March 15) ** First Usagi Lecture festival (Lunisolar February Usagi Day) * April ** Higime Lecture Society festival (Mid-April) ** Spring festival (April 28) * June ** Great Purification ceremony (June 30) * July ** Kashiwa festival (July 15) * September ** Yaejime festival (September 1) ** Mid-Autumn festival (September 14) ** '''Grand festival''' (September 15) ** Autumn festival (September 24) * November ** Meiji Day festival (November 3) * December ** Kama Purification Ritual (December 3) ** '''Grand Head festival (New Harvest festival)''' (December 10-14) ** Emperor's Birthday festival (December 23) ** Great Purification ceremony, New Year's Eve festival (December 31)
=== Grand Head festival === The Grand Head festival (Niinamesai) held from December 10 to 14 is called the "Daitōsai". The festival is led by five headmen, with the third headman being called "Daitō," giving the festival its name. The "Headman's Record" (御頭帳) traces back to Bunroku 1 (1592), making it a festival with a history of over 400 years. It is designated as an Important Intangible Folk Cultural Property of Japan. == Cultural Properties == === Selected Intangible Folk Cultural Property (National Selection) === * Headman's ceremony of Takemizuwake Shrine - Selected on December 17, 1986{{Cultural Property Database|312|353|Headman's ceremony of Takemizuwake Shrine}}. === Nagano Prefecture Designated Cultural Properties === * Nagano Prefecture Treasures (Tangible Cultural Properties) ** main hall of Kōra Shrine (Building) - Muromachi period. {{Infobox religious building|religious_affiliation = [[Shinto]]|religious_affiliation = [[Shinto]]|religious_affiliation = [[Shinto]]| religious_affiliation = [[Shinto]] | name = Takemizuwake Shrine | image = Takemizuwake-jinja shaden.JPG |caption = From right: Chokushiden, Haiden, Honden | location = {{ill|Chikuma, Nagano|ja|千曲市}}, Nagano Prefecture, Japan | coordinates = {{coord|36|31|10.08|N|138|06|10.71|E|region:JP-20_type:landmark|display=inline,title|name=Takemizuwake Shrine}} | deity = {{ill|Takemizuwake no Ōkami|ja|武美名別命}} | object = | type = {{ill|Shikinai-sha|ja|式内社}} ({{ill|Myojin Taisha|ja|名神大}})
Fourth shrine of {{ill|Shinano Province|ja|信濃国}}
Former {{ill|Prefectural shrine|ja|県社}}
{{ill|Beppyo Shrine|ja|別表神社}} | established = During the reign of the 8th Emperor {{ill|Emperor Kōgen|ja|孝元天皇}} (trad.) | architecture = Nagare-zukuri | nickname = Hachiman Shrine | pilgrimage = | festival = September 15 | rituals = Daitōsai (Niinamesai), December 10-14 | map = Japan Nagano Prefecture | label = Takemizuwake Shrine | relief = 1 | map_width = 256 }} [[File:Takemizuwake-jinja ootorii.JPG|thumb|200px|right|{{center|Ōtorii}}]] '''Takemizuwake Shrine''' (武水別神社[[ja:武水別神社]]) is a {{ill|Shinto shrine|ja|神社}} located in {{ill|Chikuma, Nagano|ja|千曲市}}, Nagano Prefecture, Japan. It is a {{ill|Shikinai-sha|ja|式内社}} ({{ill|Myojin Taisha|ja|名神大}}) and the fourth shrine of {{ill|Shinano Province|ja|信濃国}}. It was formerly classified as a {{ill|Prefectural shrine|ja|県社}} and is now a {{ill|Beppyo Shrine|ja|別表神社}} under the Association of Shinto Shrines. The shrine's old name was "Hachiman Shrine," and it is still commonly referred to as "Yawata-sama" or "Yawata Shrine." == deity == '''Main deity''' * '''{{ill|Takemizuwake no Ōkami|ja|武美名別命}}''' (Takemizuwake no Ōkami)According to the shrine's history. *: The shrine's tradition states that this deity was enshrined to pray for the fertility of the Zenkoji Plain and to prevent the flooding of the Chikuma River. '''Deities in the Same Shrine''' : The three deities enshrined together here collectively represent the {{ill|Hachiman|lt=Hachiman deity|ja|八幡神}}. * [[Emperor Ōjin|Hondawake-no-Mikoto]] (誉田別命, {{ill|Emperor Ōjin|ja|応神天皇}}) * Okinagatarashihime no Mikoto (息長足比売命, {{ill|Empress Jingū|ja|神功皇后}}) * Hime Ōkami (比咩大神) == History == === Overview === According to shrine tradition, it was established during the reign of the 8th Emperor {{ill|Emperor Kōgen|ja|孝元天皇}}Shrine history.. The earliest record in historical documents is from {{ill|Jogan|ja|貞観}} 8 (866), when it was given the rank of {{ill|Junior Second rank|ja|従二位|1=Junior Second Rank}} from no rank. Additionally, it is listed as "Takemizuwake Shrine" in the {{ill|Engishiki|ja|延喜式}} compiled in {{ill|Engi|ja|延長}} 5 (927), categorized as a {{ill|Myojin Taisha|ja|名神大}}. However, the evidence supporting the identification of this shrine as the one mentioned in the documents is not definitive『日本の神々』 Takemizuwake Shrine entry., and another candidate is {{ill|Okeno Omi Shrine|ja|桶知大神社}} in Nagano City. The area around Takemizuwake Shrine became an estate ({{ill|Shōen|ja|荘園}}) of {{ill|Iwashimizu Hachimangū|ja|石清水八幡宮}} (Otani estate) from the late Heian period, and it is said that the Hachiman deity (the three deities enshrined together) was invited from Iwashimizu Hachimangū during the Anwa era (968-970). The Hachiman deity is known as the tutelary deity of the {{ill|Minamoto clan|ja|源氏}}, and Takemizuwake Shrine was widely revered by warriors as the foremost Hachiman Shrine in the region. It is also said that {{ill|Minamoto no Yoshinaka|ja|源義仲}} prayed here『参考源平盛衰記』 mentions on June 25 (or 14), Yōwa 1 (1181), that "八幡社ヲ伏拝ミ". However, it is unclear if this "Hachiman Shrine" is the same as Takemizuwake Shrine.. In {{ill|:en:Hōgen (era)|lt=Hōgen|ja|保元}} 3 (1158), there is a record of lands in Otani estate, Sarashina District being confiscated by multiple officials. On that day, a government order was issued to halt thisIwashimizu document. During the {{ill|Nanboku-chō period|ja|南北朝時代}} (1335), the Four Shrine clan, who served as Shinto priests of Takemizuwake Shrine, together with the Hoshina and Sekiya clans, attacked the {{ill|Shugo|ja|守護所}} (provincial headquarters) in Funeiyama (Suwa), but were suppressed. This resulted in the downfall of the Four Shrine clan, who were said to have served as both {{ill|Jitō|ja|地頭}} and district officials during their peak. The shrine buildings were burned down and later rebuilt at their current location. In {{ill|Tenshō|ja|天正}} 3 (1575), {{ill|Uesugi Kenshin|ja|上杉謙信}} offered a prayer document to the shrine, praying for victory against {{ill|Hōjō Ujizane|ja|北条氏政}}{{ill|Uesugi Kenshin prayer document|ja|上杉謙信願文集}}. In {{ill|Kanei|ja|寛永}} 1 (1624), the Tokugawa shogunate granted 200 koku of shrine land to the shrine. In Meiji 1 (1868), following the separation of Shinto and Buddhism ({{ill|Shinbutsu bunri|ja|神仏分離}}), the shrine was renamed "Takemizuwake Shrine" from "Hachiman Shrine," reflecting the disbanding of the associated temple ({{ill|Shinano Five Mountains|ja|信濃五山}}). The shrine was initially classified as a village shrine ({{ill|Gōsha|ja|郷社}}) in the Modern Shrine ranking System but was promoted to a prefectural shrine ([[Ken-sha]]) in Meiji 41 (1908). In 1876, the traditional Buddhist ceremony, the Grand Head festival ({{ill|Daitōsai|ja|大頭祭}}), was transformed into a Shinto ritual吉永みち子『もっと馬を!』平凡社、1990年、8 - 20ページ「木曽馬の村」. === Shrine ranks === * Jogan 8 (866) June, promoted from no rank to Junior Second rank (『{{ill|Nihon Sandai Jitsuroku|ja|日本三代実録}}』) * Jogan 9 (867) March 26, listed as a government shrine (『日本三代実録』) == Shrine Grounds == [[File:Takemizuwake-jinja honden.JPG|thumb|210px|right|{{center|Honden}}]] [[File:Takemizuwake-jinja keidai.JPG|thumb|210px|right|{{center|Shrine Grove (Nagano Prefecture designated natural monument)}}]] The shrine grounds cover 18,896 square meters and include a grove primarily composed of zelkova and cedar trees, with over 20 species and 400 trees in total. Many of the trees are old, and the "Takemizuwake Shrine Grove" is designated as a natural monument by Nagano Prefecture. The grounds, measuring approximately 280 meters from north to south and 70 meters from east to west, were originally square but were eroded into their current rectangular shape by frequent floods from the Chikuma River. A document from the Kanei era (1624-1644) was recently discovered, showing a square layout. Most of the current shrine buildings were constructed after a fire in Tenpō 13 (1842). The main hall was completed in Kaei 3 (1850) by Tatekawa Washiro II from Suwa. The worship hall was completed in Ansei 3 (1856) by Mineura Yagorō under Tatekawa Washiro's supervision. The main hall of the subsidiary Kōra Shrine is the oldest building, having survived the fire. The associated temple, known as Sarashina Hachiman Jinguji, was one of the Shinano Five Mountains of the Tendai sect but was abolished during the Meiji period's anti-Buddhist movement ({{ill|Haibutsu kishaku|ja|廃仏毀釈}}). == Subsidiary Shrines == === Subsidiary Shrines === [[File:Takemizuwake-jinja Kora-sha.JPG|thumb|200px|right|{{center|Kōra Shrine}}{{small|The main hall inside the covering structure is a Nagano Prefecture treasure.}}]] * Kōra Shrine (高良社) *: The main hall inside the covering structure is the oldest in the shrine grounds, believed to have been built in the late Muromachi period (16th century). The shrine's old name was "Hachiman Shrine," and it is still commonly referred to as "Yawata-sama" or "Yawata Shrine." == deity == '''Main deity''' * '''{{ill|Takemizuwake no Ōkami|ja|武美名別命}}''' (Takemizuwake no Ōkami)According to the shrine's history. *: The shrine's tradition states that this deity was enshrined to pray for the fertility of the Zenkoji Plain and to prevent the flooding of the Chikuma River. '''Deities in the Same Shrine''' : The three deities enshrined together here collectively represent the {{ill|Hachiman|lt=Hachiman deity|ja|八幡神}}. * [[Emperor Ōjin|Hondawake-no-Mikoto]] (誉田別命, {{ill|Emperor Ōjin|ja|応神天皇}}) * Okinagatarashihime no Mikoto (息長足比売命, {{ill|Empress Jingū|ja|神功皇后}}) * Hime Ōkami (比咩大神) == History == === Overview === According to shrine tradition, it was established during the reign of the 8th Emperor {{ill|Emperor Kōgen|ja|孝元天皇}}Shrine history.. The earliest record in historical documents is from {{ill|Jogan|ja|貞観}} 8 (866), when it was given the rank of {{ill|Junior Second rank|ja|従二位|1=Junior Second Rank}} from no rank. Additionally, it is listed as "Takemizuwake Shrine" in the {{ill|Engishiki|ja|延喜式}} compiled in {{ill|Engi|ja|延長}} 5 (927), categorized as a {{ill|Myojin Taisha|ja|名神大}}. However, the evidence supporting the identification of this shrine as the one mentioned in the documents is not definitive『日本の神々』 Takemizuwake Shrine entry., and another candidate is {{ill|Okeno Omi Shrine|ja|桶知大神社}} in Nagano City. The area around Takemizuwake Shrine became an estate ({{ill|Shōen|ja|荘園}}) of {{ill|Iwashimizu Hachimangū|ja|石清水八幡宮}} (Otani estate) from the late Heian period, and it is said that the Hachiman deity (the three deities enshrined together) was invited from Iwashimizu Hachimangū during the Anwa era (968-970). The Hachiman deity is known as the tutelary deity of the {{ill|Minamoto clan|ja|源氏}}, and Takemizuwake Shrine was widely revered by warriors as the foremost Hachiman Shrine in the region. It is also said that {{ill|Minamoto no Yoshinaka|ja|源義仲}} prayed here『参考源平盛衰記』 mentions on June 25 (or 14), Yōwa 1 (1181), that "八幡社ヲ伏拝ミ". However, it is unclear if this "Hachiman Shrine" is the same as Takemizuwake Shrine.. In {{ill|:en:Hōgen (era)|lt=Hōgen|ja|保元}} 3 (1158), there is a record of lands in Otani estate, Sarashina District being confiscated by multiple officials. On that day, a government order was issued to halt thisIwashimizu document. During the {{ill|Nanboku-chō period|ja|南北朝時代}} (1335), the Four Shrine clan, who served as Shinto priests of Takemizuwake Shrine, together with the Hoshina and Sekiya clans, attacked the {{ill|Shugo|ja|守護所}} (provincial headquarters) in Funeiyama (Suwa), but were suppressed. This resulted in the downfall of the Four Shrine clan, who were said to have served as both {{ill|Jitō|ja|地頭}} and district officials during their peak. The shrine buildings were burned down and later rebuilt at their current location. In {{ill|Tenshō|ja|天正}} 3 (1575), {{ill|Uesugi Kenshin|ja|上杉謙信}} offered a prayer document to the shrine, praying for victory against {{ill|Hōjō Ujizane|ja|北条氏政}}{{ill|Uesugi Kenshin prayer document|ja|上杉謙信願文集}}. In {{ill|Kanei|ja|寛永}} 1 (1624), the Tokugawa shogunate granted 200 koku of shrine land to the shrine. In Meiji 1 (1868), following the separation of Shinto and Buddhism ({{ill|Shinbutsu bunri|ja|神仏分離}}), the shrine was renamed "Takemizuwake Shrine" from "Hachiman Shrine," reflecting the disbanding of the associated temple ({{ill|Shinano Five Mountains|ja|信濃五山}}). The shrine was initially classified as a village shrine ({{ill|Gōsha|ja|郷社}}) in the Modern Shrine ranking System but was promoted to a prefectural shrine ([[Ken-sha]]) in Meiji 41 (1908). In 1876, the traditional Buddhist ceremony, the Grand Head festival ({{ill|Daitōsai|ja|大頭祭}}), was transformed into a Shinto ritual吉永みち子『もっと馬を!』平凡社、1990年、8 - 20ページ「木曽馬の村」. === Shrine ranks === * Jogan 8 (866) June, promoted from no rank to Junior Second rank (『{{ill|Nihon Sandai Jitsuroku|ja|日本三代実録}}』) * Jogan 9 (867) March 26, listed as a government shrine (『日本三代実録』) == Shrine Grounds == [[File:Takemizuwake-jinja honden.JPG|thumb|210px|right|{{center|Honden}}]] [[File:Takemizuwake-jinja keidai.JPG|thumb|210px|right|{{center|Shrine Grove (Nagano Prefecture designated natural monument)}}]] The shrine grounds cover 18,896 square meters and include a grove primarily composed of zelkova and cedar trees, with over 20 species and 400 trees in total. Many of the trees are old, and the "Takemizuwake Shrine Grove" is designated as a natural monument by Nagano Prefecture. The grounds, measuring approximately 280 meters from north to south and 70 meters from east to west, were originally square but were eroded into their current rectangular shape by frequent floods from the Chikuma River. A document from the Kanei era (1624-1644) was recently discovered, showing a square layout. Most of the current shrine buildings were constructed after a fire in Tenpō 13 (1842). The main hall was completed in Kaei 3 (1850) by Tatekawa Washiro II from Suwa. The worship hall was completed in Ansei 3 (1856) by Mineura Yagorō under Tatekawa Washiro's supervision. The main hall of the subsidiary Kōra Shrine is the oldest building, having survived the fire. The associated temple, known as Sarashina Hachiman Jinguji, was one of the Shinano Five Mountains of the Tendai sect but was abolished during the Meiji period's anti-Buddhist movement ({{ill|Haibutsu kishaku|ja|廃仏毀釈}}). == Subsidiary Shrines == === Subsidiary Shrines === [[File:Takemizuwake-jinja Kora-sha.JPG|thumb|200px|right|{{center|Kōra Shrine}}{{small|The main hall inside the covering structure is a Nagano Prefecture treasure.}}]] * Kōra Shrine (高良社) *: The main hall inside the covering structure is the oldest in the shrine grounds, believed to have been built in the late Muromachi period (16th century). {{Infobox religious building|religious_affiliation = [[Shinto]]|religious_affiliation = [[Shinto]]|religious_affiliation = [[Shinto]]| religious_affiliation = [[Shinto]] | name = Takemizuwake Shrine | image = Takemizuwake-jinja shaden.JPG |caption = From right: Chokushiden, Haiden, Honden | location = {{ill|Chikuma, Nagano|ja|千曲市}}, Nagano Prefecture, Japan | coordinates = {{coord|36|31|10.08|N|138|06|10.71|E|region:JP-20_type:landmark|display=inline,title|name=Takemizuwake Shrine}} | deity = {{ill|Takemizuwake no Ōkami|ja|武美名別命}} | object = | type = {{ill|Shikinai-sha|ja|式内社}} ({{ill|Myojin Taisha|ja|名神大}})
Fourth shrine of {{ill|Shinano Province|ja|信濃国}}
Former {{ill|Prefectural shrine|ja|県社}}
{{ill|Beppyo Shrine|ja|別表神社}} | established = During the reign of the 8th Emperor {{ill|Emperor Kōgen|ja|孝元天皇}} (trad.) | architecture = Nagare-zukuri | nickname = Hachiman Shrine | pilgrimage = | festival = September 15 | rituals = Daitōsai (Niinamesai), December 10-14 | map = Japan Nagano Prefecture | label = Takemizuwake Shrine | relief = 1 | map_width = 256 }} [[File:Takemizuwake-jinja ootorii.JPG|thumb|200px|right|{{center|Ōtorii}}]] '''Takemizuwake Shrine''' (武水別神社[[ja:武水別神社]]) is a {{ill|Shinto shrine|ja|神社}} located in {{ill|Chikuma, Nagano|ja|千曲市}}, Nagano Prefecture, Japan. It is a {{ill|Shikinai-sha|ja|式内社}} ({{ill|Myojin Taisha|ja|名神大}}) and the fourth shrine of {{ill|Shinano Province|ja|信濃国}}. It was formerly classified as a {{ill|Prefectural shrine|ja|県社}} and is now a {{ill|Beppyo Shrine|ja|別表神社}} under the Association of Shinto Shrines. The shrine's old name was "Hachiman Shrine," and it is still commonly referred to as "Yawata-sama" or "Yawata Shrine." == deity == '''Main deity''' * '''{{ill|Takemizuwake no Ōkami|ja|武美名別命}}''' (Takemizuwake no Ōkami)According to the shrine's history. *: The shrine's tradition states that this deity was enshrined to pray for the fertility of the Zenkoji Plain and to prevent the flooding of the Chikuma River. '''Deities in the Same Shrine''' : The three deities enshrined together here collectively represent the {{ill|Hachiman|lt=Hachiman deity|ja|八幡神}}. * [[Emperor Ōjin|Hondawake-no-Mikoto]] (誉田別命, {{ill|Emperor Ōjin|ja|応神天皇}}) * Okinagatarashihime no Mikoto (息長足比売命, {{ill|Empress Jingū|ja|神功皇后}}) * Hime Ōkami (比咩大神) == History == === Overview === According to shrine tradition, it was established during the reign of the 8th Emperor {{ill|Emperor Kōgen|ja|孝元天皇}}Shrine history.. The earliest record in historical documents is from {{ill|Jogan|ja|貞観}} 8 (866), when it was given the rank of {{ill|Junior Second rank|ja|従二位|1=Junior Second Rank}} from no rank. Additionally, it is listed as "Takemizuwake Shrine" in the {{ill|Engishiki|ja|延喜式}} compiled in {{ill|Engi|ja|延長}} 5 (927), categorized as a {{ill|Myojin Taisha|ja|名神大}}. However, the evidence supporting the identification of this shrine as the one mentioned in the documents is not definitive『日本の神々』 Takemizuwake Shrine entry., and another candidate is {{ill|Okeno Omi Shrine|ja|桶知大神社}} in Nagano City. The area around Takemizuwake Shrine became an estate ({{ill|Shōen|ja|荘園}}) of {{ill|Iwashimizu Hachimangū|ja|石清水八幡宮}} (Otani estate) from the late Heian period, and it is said that the Hachiman deity (the three deities enshrined together) was invited from Iwashimizu Hachimangū during the Anwa era (968-970). The Hachiman deity is known as the tutelary deity of the {{ill|Minamoto clan|ja|源氏}}, and Takemizuwake Shrine was widely revered by warriors as the foremost Hachiman Shrine in the region. It is also said that {{ill|Minamoto no Yoshinaka|ja|源義仲}} prayed here『参考源平盛衰記』 mentions on June 25 (or 14), Yōwa 1 (1181), that "八幡社ヲ伏拝ミ". However, it is unclear if this "Hachiman Shrine" is the same as Takemizuwake Shrine.. In {{ill|:en:Hōgen (era)|lt=Hōgen|ja|保元}} 3 (1158), there is a record of lands in Otani estate, Sarashina District being confiscated by multiple officials. On that day, a government order was issued to halt thisIwashimizu document. During the {{ill|Nanboku-chō period|ja|南北朝時代}} (1335), the Four Shrine clan, who served as Shinto priests of Takemizuwake Shrine, together with the Hoshina and Sekiya clans, attacked the {{ill|Shugo|ja|守護所}} (provincial headquarters) in Funeiyama (Suwa), but were suppressed. This resulted in the downfall of the Four Shrine clan, who were said to have served as both {{ill|Jitō|ja|地頭}} and district officials during their peak. The shrine buildings were burned down and later rebuilt at their current location. In {{ill|Tenshō|ja|天正}} 3 (1575), {{ill|Uesugi Kenshin|ja|上杉謙信}} offered a prayer document to the shrine, praying for victory against {{ill|Hōjō Ujizane|ja|北条氏政}}{{ill|Uesugi Kenshin prayer document|ja|上杉謙信願文集}}. In {{ill|Kanei|ja|寛永}} 1 (1624), the Tokugawa shogunate granted 200 koku of shrine land to the shrine. In Meiji 1 (1868), following the separation of Shinto and Buddhism ({{ill|Shinbutsu bunri|ja|神仏分離}}), the shrine was renamed "Takemizuwake Shrine" from "Hachiman Shrine," reflecting the disbanding of the associated temple ({{ill|Shinano Five Mountains|ja|信濃五山}}). The shrine was initially classified as a village shrine ({{ill|Gōsha|ja|郷社}}) in the Modern Shrine ranking System but was promoted to a prefectural shrine ([[Ken-sha]]) in Meiji 41 (1908). In 1876, the traditional Buddhist ceremony, the Grand Head festival ({{ill|Daitōsai|ja|大頭祭}}), was transformed into a Shinto ritual吉永みち子『もっと馬を!』平凡社、1990年、8 - 20ページ「木曽馬の村」. === Shrine ranks === * Jogan 8 (866) June, promoted from no rank to Junior Second rank (『{{ill|Nihon Sandai Jitsuroku|ja|日本三代実録}}』) * Jogan 9 (867) March 26, listed as a government shrine (『日本三代実録』) == Shrine Grounds == [[File:Takemizuwake-jinja honden.JPG|thumb|210px|right|{{center|Honden}}]] [[File:Takemizuwake-jinja keidai.JPG|thumb|210px|right|{{center|Shrine Grove (Nagano Prefecture designated natural monument)}}]] The shrine grounds cover 18,896 square meters and include a grove primarily composed of zelkova and cedar trees, with over 20 species and 400 trees in total. Many of the trees are old, and the "Takemizuwake Shrine Grove" is designated as a natural monument by Nagano Prefecture. The grounds, measuring approximately 280 meters from north to south and 70 meters from east to west, were originally square but were eroded into their current rectangular shape by frequent floods from the Chikuma River. A document from the Kanei era (1624-1644) was recently discovered, showing a square layout. Most of the current shrine buildings were constructed after a fire in Tenpō 13 (1842). The main hall was completed in Kaei 3 (1850) by Tatekawa Washiro II from Suwa. The worship hall was completed in Ansei 3 (1856) by Mineura Yagorō under Tatekawa Washiro's supervision. The main hall of the subsidiary Kōra Shrine is the oldest building, having survived the fire. The associated temple, known as Sarashina Hachiman Jinguji, was one of the Shinano Five Mountains of the Tendai sect but was abolished during the Meiji period's anti-Buddhist movement ({{ill|Haibutsu kishaku|ja|廃仏毀釈}}). == Subsidiary Shrines == === Subsidiary Shrines === [[File:Takemizuwake-jinja Kora-sha.JPG|thumb|200px|right|{{center|Kōra Shrine}}{{small|The main hall inside the covering structure is a Nagano Prefecture treasure.}}]] * Kōra Shrine (高良社) *: The main hall inside the covering structure is the oldest in the shrine grounds, believed to have been built in the late Muromachi period (16th century). It is designated as a Nagano Prefecture treasureExplanatory panel on-site.. === Associated Shrines === * Emperor Jimmu Shrine * Smallpox Shrine * Sake Brewer Shrine * Yaegaki Shrine * Sukune Shrine * Komagata Shrine * Kojin Shrine * Twelve Shrines * Tenjin Shrine * Koyasu Shrine * Ten stone shrines: Ontake Shrine, Kotohira Shrine, Tōshōgū, Myōgi Shrine, Seki no Kami, Dōsojin, Water God Shrine, Mountain God Shrine, Akiba Shrine, Kashima Shrine == festivals == === festivals === The festivals held at Takemizuwake Shrine are as follows. Particularly notable are the three major festivals: the Prayer festival (March 15), the Grand festival (September 15), and the Grand Head festival (New Harvest festival, December 10-14).
festivals List
The three major festivals are in boldfestivals according to the shrine history.. * Monthly ** Monthly festival (1st, 5th, 28th) ** Usagi Day festival (Usagi Day) * January ** New Year's festival (January 1) ** Rice Planting festival (January 5) ** New Year's festival (January 15) * February ** Setsubun festival (Setsubun Day in February) ** National Foundation Day festival (February 11) * March ** '''Prayer festival''' (March 15) ** First Usagi Lecture festival (Lunisolar February Usagi Day) * April ** Higime Lecture Society festival (Mid-April) ** Spring festival (April 28) * June ** Great Purification ceremony (June 30) * July ** Kashiwa festival (July 15) * September ** Yaejime festival (September 1) ** Mid-Autumn festival (September 14) ** '''Grand festival''' (September 15) ** Autumn festival (September 24) * November ** Meiji Day festival (November 3) * December ** Kama Purification Ritual (December 3) ** '''Grand Head festival (New Harvest festival)''' (December 10-14) ** Emperor's Birthday festival (December 23) ** Great Purification ceremony, New Year's Eve festival (December 31)
=== Grand Head festival === The Grand Head festival (Niinamesai) held from December 10 to 14 is called the "Daitōsai". The festival is led by five headmen, with the third headman being called "Daitō," giving the festival its name. The "Headman's Record" (御頭帳) traces back to Bunroku 1 (1592), making it a festival with a history of over 400 years. It is designated as an Important Intangible Folk Cultural Property of Japan. == Cultural Properties == === Selected Intangible Folk Cultural Property (National Selection) === * Headman's ceremony of Takemizuwake Shrine - Selected on December 17, 1986{{Cultural Property Database|312|353|Headman's ceremony of Takemizuwake Shrine}}. === Nagano Prefecture Designated Cultural Properties === * Nagano Prefecture Treasures (Tangible Cultural Properties) ** main hall of Kōra Shrine (Building) - Muromachi period. This resulted in the downfall of the Four Shrine clan, who were said to have served as both {{ill|Jitō|ja|地頭}} and district officials during their peak. The shrine buildings were burned down and later rebuilt at their current location. In {{ill|Tenshō|ja|天正}} 3 (1575), {{ill|Uesugi Kenshin|ja|上杉謙信}} offered a prayer document to the shrine, praying for victory against {{ill|Hōjō Ujizane|ja|北条氏政}}{{ill|Uesugi Kenshin prayer document|ja|上杉謙信願文集}}. In {{ill|Kanei|ja|寛永}} 1 (1624), the Tokugawa shogunate granted 200 koku of shrine land to the shrine. In Meiji 1 (1868), following the separation of Shinto and Buddhism ({{ill|Shinbutsu bunri|ja|神仏分離}}), the shrine was renamed "Takemizuwake Shrine" from "Hachiman Shrine," reflecting the disbanding of the associated temple ({{ill|Shinano Five Mountains|ja|信濃五山}}). The shrine was initially classified as a village shrine ({{ill|Gōsha|ja|郷社}}) in the Modern Shrine ranking System but was promoted to a prefectural shrine ([[Ken-sha]]) in Meiji 41 (1908). In 1876, the traditional Buddhist ceremony, the Grand Head festival ({{ill|Daitōsai|ja|大頭祭}}), was transformed into a Shinto ritual吉永みち子『もっと馬を!』平凡社、1990年、8 - 20ページ「木曽馬の村」. === Shrine ranks === * Jogan 8 (866) June, promoted from no rank to Junior Second rank (『{{ill|Nihon Sandai Jitsuroku|ja|日本三代実録}}』) * Jogan 9 (867) March 26, listed as a government shrine (『日本三代実録』) == Shrine Grounds == [[File:Takemizuwake-jinja honden.JPG|thumb|210px|right|{{center|Honden}}]] [[File:Takemizuwake-jinja keidai.JPG|thumb|210px|right|{{center|Shrine Grove (Nagano Prefecture designated natural monument)}}]] The shrine grounds cover 18,896 square meters and include a grove primarily composed of zelkova and cedar trees, with over 20 species and 400 trees in total. Many of the trees are old, and the "Takemizuwake Shrine Grove" is designated as a natural monument by Nagano Prefecture. The grounds, measuring approximately 280 meters from north to south and 70 meters from east to west, were originally square but were eroded into their current rectangular shape by frequent floods from the Chikuma River. A document from the Kanei era (1624-1644) was recently discovered, showing a square layout. Most of the current shrine buildings were constructed after a fire in Tenpō 13 (1842). The main hall was completed in Kaei 3 (1850) by Tatekawa Washiro II from Suwa. The worship hall was completed in Ansei 3 (1856) by Mineura Yagorō under Tatekawa Washiro's supervision. The main hall of the subsidiary Kōra Shrine is the oldest building, having survived the fire. The associated temple, known as Sarashina Hachiman Jinguji, was one of the Shinano Five Mountains of the Tendai sect but was abolished during the Meiji period's anti-Buddhist movement ({{ill|Haibutsu kishaku|ja|廃仏毀釈}}). == Subsidiary Shrines == === Subsidiary Shrines === [[File:Takemizuwake-jinja Kora-sha.JPG|thumb|200px|right|{{center|Kōra Shrine}}{{small|The main hall inside the covering structure is a Nagano Prefecture treasure.}}]] * Kōra Shrine (高良社) *: The main hall inside the covering structure is the oldest in the shrine grounds, believed to have been built in the late Muromachi period (16th century). {{ill|Beppyo Shrine|ja|別表神社}} | established = During the reign of the 8th Emperor {{ill|Emperor Kōgen|ja|孝元天皇}} (trad.) | architecture = Nagare-zukuri | nickname = Hachiman Shrine | pilgrimage = | festival = September 15 | rituals = Daitōsai (Niinamesai), December 10-14 | map = Japan Nagano Prefecture | label = Takemizuwake Shrine | relief = 1 | map_width = 256 }} [[File:Takemizuwake-jinja ootorii.JPG|thumb|200px|right|{{center|Ōtorii}}]] '''Takemizuwake Shrine''' (武水別神社[[ja:武水別神社]]) is a {{ill|Shinto shrine|ja|神社}} located in {{ill|Chikuma, Nagano|ja|千曲市}}, Nagano Prefecture, Japan. It is a {{ill|Shikinai-sha|ja|式内社}} ({{ill|Myojin Taisha|ja|名神大}}) and the fourth shrine of {{ill|Shinano Province|ja|信濃国}}. It was formerly classified as a {{ill|Prefectural shrine|ja|県社}} and is now a {{ill|Beppyo Shrine|ja|別表神社}} under the Association of Shinto Shrines. The shrine's old name was "Hachiman Shrine," and it is still commonly referred to as "Yawata-sama" or "Yawata Shrine." == deity == '''Main deity''' * '''{{ill|Takemizuwake no Ōkami|ja|武美名別命}}''' (Takemizuwake no Ōkami)According to the shrine's history. *: The shrine's tradition states that this deity was enshrined to pray for the fertility of the Zenkoji Plain and to prevent the flooding of the Chikuma River. '''Deities in the Same Shrine''' : The three deities enshrined together here collectively represent the {{ill|Hachiman|lt=Hachiman deity|ja|八幡神}}. * [[Emperor Ōjin|Hondawake-no-Mikoto]] (誉田別命, {{ill|Emperor Ōjin|ja|応神天皇}}) * Okinagatarashihime no Mikoto (息長足比売命, {{ill|Empress Jingū|ja|神功皇后}}) * Hime Ōkami (比咩大神) == History == === Overview === According to shrine tradition, it was established during the reign of the 8th Emperor {{ill|Emperor Kōgen|ja|孝元天皇}}Shrine history.. The earliest record in historical documents is from {{ill|Jogan|ja|貞観}} 8 (866), when it was given the rank of {{ill|Junior Second rank|ja|従二位|1=Junior Second Rank}} from no rank. Additionally, it is listed as "Takemizuwake Shrine" in the {{ill|Engishiki|ja|延喜式}} compiled in {{ill|Engi|ja|延長}} 5 (927), categorized as a {{ill|Myojin Taisha|ja|名神大}}. However, the evidence supporting the identification of this shrine as the one mentioned in the documents is not definitive『日本の神々』 Takemizuwake Shrine entry., and another candidate is {{ill|Okeno Omi Shrine|ja|桶知大神社}} in Nagano City. The area around Takemizuwake Shrine became an estate ({{ill|Shōen|ja|荘園}}) of {{ill|Iwashimizu Hachimangū|ja|石清水八幡宮}} (Otani estate) from the late Heian period, and it is said that the Hachiman deity (the three deities enshrined together) was invited from Iwashimizu Hachimangū during the Anwa era (968-970). The Hachiman deity is known as the tutelary deity of the {{ill|Minamoto clan|ja|源氏}}, and Takemizuwake Shrine was widely revered by warriors as the foremost Hachiman Shrine in the region. It is also said that {{ill|Minamoto no Yoshinaka|ja|源義仲}} prayed here『参考源平盛衰記』 mentions on June 25 (or 14), Yōwa 1 (1181), that "八幡社ヲ伏拝ミ". However, it is unclear if this "Hachiman Shrine" is the same as Takemizuwake Shrine.. In {{ill|:en:Hōgen (era)|lt=Hōgen|ja|保元}} 3 (1158), there is a record of lands in Otani estate, Sarashina District being confiscated by multiple officials. On that day, a government order was issued to halt thisIwashimizu document.
